In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we identified p38α as an important molecule in the resistance of leukemia cells to the topoisomeras IIα inhibitor MX2.

the MX2 resistant cell line was globally hypomethylated and the methylation of the p38α promoter was responsible for altered expression of p38 mRNA and protein, which was associated with increased p38 kinase activity.

the genome‐wide DNA methyloproteome of MX2‐resistance in leukemia cells is characterized by a global hypermethylation of CpG islands, and that this methylation‐related gene silencing is involved in altered gene expression and drug resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified p38α as an enzyme involved in MX‐related drug resistance and that blocking the p38α pathway could restore the sensitivity to MX in resistant cells.

the genome‐wide analysis of DNA methylation in resistant leukemia cells revealed that the methylation of CpG islands was globally increased in MX2‐resistance, and the p38α gene was hypermethylated and silenced in the resistant cell line.
we identified a novel target for drug resistance in leukemia cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p38 kinase activity was increased in MX2‐resistance and that inhibition of p38 kinase activity by a specific inhibitor or by siRNA restored MX2‐sensitivity.
